agree.reason: The speech is personal and well organized, but the two commissioners worried about traffic only get told that a D grade 'isn't the road stopping' and a vague 'consider a condition', not the funded signal that keeps the intersection at C, so the resisting reader has little reason to change their vote.

honest.reason: The figures are accurate and 'one in six' is a fair rounding of 64/412, but 'I drive through that intersection all the time' is an invented detail, and saying a D 'just means a longer wait' plays down the impact a little.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out useful figures (one in six of the waitlist, eight spare parking spaces) and makes good use of the lot sitting empty six days a week, but it never uses the strongest available fact, that the signal keeps the intersection at C.

right_comparison.reason: The 'if you say no' paragraph sets out the status quo fairly (empty lot, a 2,100-home shortfall, families still waiting), but it doesn't add that approval with the signal would leave traffic at grade C, so the trade-off looks worse than it is.

qualification.reason: The only condition is a vague 'if you believe the intersection needs improvement', when the speaker's actual ask is approval conditioned on a specific, builder-funded signal that the study says holds the C rating.

objections.reason: Parking and the loss of open space are dealt with, but the main traffic objection gets a shrug instead of the signal, and the speech doesn't mention 20 months of construction trucks, neighbour weekday parking, or the neighbour group the speaker could commit to.

fit.reason: It's in the right first-person speech form, but at about 470 words it runs close to or past three minutes, and repeating the 'nineteen years' line spends time that the missing commitments needed.
